items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with a countable complete orthonormal family $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$, let $\beta>0$, and let
$F(H)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Let
$\mathcal M$ be the set of finite nondecreasing sequences
$I=(j_1\le\cdots\le j_n)$ with $n\ge0$ (the empty sequence included); for
$I=(j_1\le\cdots\le j_n)$ put
$$v_I:=P_+^{(n)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_n})\in F(H)\quad(n\ge1),\qquad v_{\varnothing}:=\Omega,\qquad \lambda_I:=\varepsilon_{j_1}+\cdots+\varepsilon_{j_n}\ (\text{empty sum }0),$$
and $u_I:=v_I/\|v_I\|$. Then:

(a) $(u_I)_{I\in\mathcal M}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(H)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]);

(b) the diagonal operator
$$D(D_\beta):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-2\beta\lambda_I}|\langle\psi,u_I\rangle|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad D_\beta\psi:=\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}\langle\psi,u_I\rangle u_I$$
is bounded, self-adjoint and positive with $\|D_\beta\|\le1$; it is trace class
exactly when $\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}<\infty$, and then
$\operatorname{tr}D_\beta=\sum_Ie^{-\beta\lambda_I}$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);

(c) for every $N\ge1$, $\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{I\in\mathcal M\\ I\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}}}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\prod_{j=1}^N\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}$, and
$$\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\lim_{N\to\infty}\prod_{j=1}^N\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}\in(0,\infty];$$

(d) *product criterion*: $\sum_{I}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}<\infty$ if and only if
$\sum_{j\ge1}e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, and in that case
$$\sum_{I\in\mathcal M}e^{-\beta\lambda_I}=\prod_{j=1}^\infty\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}}<\infty ;$$

(e) consequently $D_\beta$ is trace class if and only if
$\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty$, with the trace given by the infinite
product in (d).

The operator $D_\beta$ is a purely mathematical diagonal operator on $F(H)$;
no thermal, thermodynamic or measurement interpretation is asserted.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\beta>0$ and let $(\varepsilon_j)_{j\ge1}\subseteq(0,\infty)$ and
$\mu\in\mathbb R$ be real data; write $q_j:=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)}$.

(a) *Single fermionic orbital.* On $\mathfrak h:=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal
basis $(u_0,u_1)$ define the bounded self-adjoint operator $N_-$ by
$N_-u_0=0$, $N_-u_1=u_1$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Then the diagonal
operator $F:=\sum_{k=0}^1e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}\,T_{u_k,u_k}$ is
positive, self-adjoint, finite rank, and
$$\operatorname{tr}F=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)},\qquad \frac{\sum_{k=0}^1k\,e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)k}}{\operatorname{tr}F}=\frac1{e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1}$$
([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]],
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

(b) *Countable grand-canonical factor products.* Define
$\mathcal N:=\{N\subseteq\{1,2,\dots\}:N\text{ finite}\}$ and set
$$Z_{\mathrm B}:=\sup_{N\in\mathcal N}\ \prod_{j\in N}\frac1{1-q_j}\in(0,\infty],\qquad Z_{\mathrm F}:=\sup_{N\in\mathcal N}\ \prod_{j\in N}(1+q_j)\in[1,\infty],$$
with the convention $Z_{\mathrm B}:=+\infty$ if some $j$ has
$\varepsilon_j-\mu\le0$. Then:
$$Z_{\mathrm B}<\infty\iff\sum_j e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty \ \text{ and }\ \mu<\inf_j\varepsilon_j,\qquad Z_{\mathrm F}<\infty\iff\sum_je^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty,$$
and in these finite cases $Z_{\mathrm B}=\prod_{j\ge1}(1-q_j)^{-1}$ and
$Z_{\mathrm F}=\prod_{j\ge1}(1+q_j)$.

(c) *Mode occupancies and dilute remainders.* For a single mode with
$0<q<1$ (boson) and $q>0$ (fermion),
$$\frac{\sum_{n\ge0}n\,q^n}{\sum_{n\ge0}q^n}=\frac q{1-q}=q+\frac{q^2}{1-q},\qquad \frac{\sum_{n=0}^1n\,q^n}{\sum_{n=0}^1q^n}=\frac q{1+q}=q-\frac{q^2}{1+q};$$
consequently the deviations from $q$ are bounded by $q^2/(1-q)$ and
$q^2/(1+q)$ respectively, and both are at most $2q^2$ when $q\le1/2$.

All statements are mathematical statements about diagonal weights and products;
no identification of $\beta,\mu,\varepsilon_j$ with physical temperatures,
chemical potentials or energies, and no thermal or thermodynamic conclusion,
is asserted.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $N\ge1$ and $r\ge1$,
let $m_1,\dots,m_N>0$, $\hbar>0$, let $a_1,\dots,a_M\in\mathbb R^3$ be fixed
points, and let $z_{im},z_{ij}\in\mathbb R$ be real coefficients
($1\le i\le N$, $1\le m\le M$, $1\le i<j\le N$). Let $K$ be the free kinetic
operator of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]],
$D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$ with equivalent graph norm, and define
the singular multiplier
$$V(X):=\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{m=1}^M\frac{z_{im}}{|x_i-a_m|}+\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac{z_{ij}}{|x_i-x_j|},\qquad X=(x_1,\dots,x_N)\in\mathbb R^{3N},$$
as an a.e.-defined real measurable function
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). Then:

(a) each of the multipliers $u\mapsto u/|x_i-a_m|$ and
$u\mapsto u/|x_i-x_j|$ is $K$-bounded with $K$-bound zero: for every
$\eta>0$ there is a finite constant $C_\eta$ with
$$\Bigl\|\frac{u}{|x_i-a_m|}\Bigr\|_2\le\eta\|Ku\|_2+C_\eta\|u\|_2,\qquad \Bigl\|\frac{u}{|x_i-x_j|}\Bigr\|_2\le\eta\|Ku\|_2+C_\eta\|u\|_2$$
for all $u\in D(K)$ ([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]],
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]);

(b) $D(K)\subseteq D(M_V)$, and $M_V$ is symmetric on $D(K)$ with $K$-bound
zero; consequently
$$H:=K+M_V,\qquad D(H):=D(K)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C),$$
is self-adjoint and bounded below, and $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$
is a core for $H$ ([[thm-kato-rellich]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(c) the operator $K\otimes I_r+M_V\otimes I_r$ on
$L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)\otimes\mathbb C^r$ with domain $D(K)\otimes\mathbb C^r$
is self-adjoint and bounded below;

(d) if $m_1=\cdots=m_N=m$ and the coefficients are permutation invariant
($z_{im}$ independent of $i$ and $z_{ij}$ independent of the pair), then the
transported permutation unitaries of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]]
reduce $H$, and the restrictions of $H$ to the symmetric and antisymmetric
sectors are self-adjoint on those sectors.

No Hunziker-van Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no uniform-in-$N$
stability, no thermodynamic limit, no spectral statement beyond
self-adjointness and boundedness from below, and no physical interpretation of
$H$, the masses or the coefficients is asserted.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric
projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]). Then:

(a) *Slater vectors*: for $n\ge2$ and orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_n\in H$, the
Slater vector
$$S(u_1,\dots,u_n):=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\,u_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\sigma(n)}$$
satisfies $\|S(u_1,\dots,u_n)\|=1$ and
$S(u_1,\dots,u_n)=\sqrt{n!}\,P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)$;

(b) *exclusion*: if $u_i=u_j$ for some $i\ne j$, then
$P_-^{(n)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n)=0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] (d));

(c) *two orbitals, bounded pair interaction*: let $u,v\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be normalized and orthogonal, let $W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and
bounded with $W(-z)=W(z)$ for a.e. $z$, let
$\Theta:L^2(\mathbb R^3)\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ be the
Euclidean product unitary
([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]), put
$\varphi_\pm:=(u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u)/\sqrt2$ and
$$D:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X:=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,$$
integrals of absolutely integrable functions. Then $D,X\in\mathbb R$ and the
pair expectation of the multiplier $M_W$ in the two spatial states is
$$\bigl\langle M_W(\Theta\varphi_\pm),\Theta\varphi_\pm\bigr\rangle=D\pm X .$$

(d) *repulsive Coulomb exchange*: let $\kappa>0$, $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$, let
$u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\cap L^2$ be normalized and orthogonal
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
The vectors $\Theta\varphi_\pm$ belong to $D(M_W)$: Hardy translated in the $y$ variable and Tonelli give $\iint|u(x)v(y)|^2/|x-y|^2\le4\|u\|_2^2\|\nabla v\|_2^2<\infty$, and the swapped product has the same property. Then the integrals $D$ and $X$ converge absolutely, $0\le D<\infty$,
$X\in\mathbb R$ with $X\ge0$; consequently
$D-X\le D+X$, i.e. the antisymmetric spatial pair state has the lower
expectation of the repulsive Coulomb pair interaction.

The exchange calculation is a statement about the indicated spatial vectors; it
does not deduce the spin-statistics assignment of any species, and combining the
spatial states with spin requires a separately stipulated symmetry rule. No
physical interpretation of $D$, $X$ or the states is asserted.

items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Adopt the objects and
hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]:
$d\ge1$, Hermitian matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ on $\mathbb C^d$, cutoff
$\Lambda>0$, transverse vectors $g_j$ with
$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{0<\varepsilon\le\Lambda\}$ and
$g_j/\sqrt\varepsilon\in\mathfrak h$, coupling $\eta_0\in\mathbb R$,
$$H_0:=H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_f,\qquad B:=\eta_0\sum_{j=1}^JD_j\otimes\phi(g_j),\qquad H:=H_0+B,$$
all with domain $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$ so that $H_0$ and $H$ are self-adjoint on
that domain. Fix $\hbar>0$, a unit vector $v_a\in\mathbb C^d$ and
$\Psi_0:=v_a\otimes\Omega$, and define the interaction-picture family
$$V(t):=e^{itH_0/\hbar}Be^{-itH_0/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
For $n\ge0$ and $t\ge0$ let
$$\Psi_n(t):=\Bigl(\frac1{i\hbar}\Bigr)^{\!n}\int_{0<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}V(t_n)\cdots V(t_1)\Psi_0\,dt_1\cdots dt_n$$
(iterated Bochner integral in $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$; $\Psi_0(t):=\Psi_0$). Put
$C:=2\sum_{j=1}^J\|D_j\|\,\|g_j\|/\hbar$ and $C':=C\Lambda$. Then:

(a) for all $n\ge0$ and $t\ge0$,
$$\|\Psi_n(t)\|\le\frac{(|\eta_0|Ct)^n}{\sqrt{n!}};$$

(b) the vectors $\Psi_n(t)$ lie in $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$, the series
$\sum_{n\ge0}\Psi_n(t)$ converges in the graph norm of $H_f$ uniformly for $t$
in compact subsets of $[0,\infty)$, and its sum $\Psi(t)$ satisfies
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\Psi(t)=V(t)\Psi(t),\qquad \Psi(0)=\Psi_0 ;$$

(c) the Dyson sum solves the actual self-adjoint evolution:
$e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0$ for every $t\ge0$;

(d) explicit tail bound: for $0\le t\le T$ and $N\ge1$,
$$\Bigl\|e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0-e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Psi_n(t)\Bigr\|\le\sum_{n\ge N}\frac{(|\eta_0|CT)^n}{\sqrt{n!}} .$$

The convergence is proved for the actual self-adjoint $H$ on the stated domain;
this is not a formal manipulation of divergent series, and no all-time
weak-coupling, Markov or exponential-decay statement is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the cutoff data, self-adjoint $H_0,H$ on $\mathcal G:=\mathbb C^d\otimes D(H_f)$, $F:=I\otimes H_f$, $B:=\eta_0\sum_jD_j\otimes\phi(g_j)$, $U_0(t):=e^{itH_0/\hbar}$, $V(t):=U_0(t)BU_0(-t)$, and the vacuum initial vector. Put $\|x\|_{\mathcal G}:=\|x\|+\|Fx\|$; let $\mathcal K_m$ be the closed subspace with photon numbers at most $m$, including the atomic factor, and $\mathcal G_m:=\mathcal G\cap\mathcal K_m$. Define the coupling-independent constant $\gamma:=2\sum_j\|D_j\|\,\|g_j\|$, so $C=\gamma/\hbar$.

[F1] The cutoff relative-bound theorem gives symmetry of $B$, its relative bound zero, and self-adjointness of $H_0,H$ on $\mathcal G$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] (a)-(c)). In particular $B:\mathcal G\to\mathcal K$ is bounded for the graph norm, where $\mathcal K=\mathbb C^d\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$; since $H_0-F$ is bounded, the two graph norms are equivalent.

[F2] The sector formulas give $\|A_\pm(g)x\|\le\sqrt{m+1}\|g\|\|x\|$ on $\mathcal K_m$, and each changes photon number by one; their sum has bound $2\sqrt{m+1}\|g\|$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] (b),(c), [[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]] (a),(b)). Contraction is conjugate-linear in its vector argument and satisfies $\Psi_g(u\otimes z)=\langle u,g\rangle z$.

[F3] The free field operator is the positive closed sector sum with multiplier $\sum_i\varepsilon(k_i)$, and $H_f\Omega=0$. Its sector projections commute with its unitary group ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]] (a)-(c)). The Euclidean product identification, tensor density and permutation formulas are [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. AC supplies any DC prerequisite of the free-field supplier ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F4] A finite Hermitian matrix has an orthonormal eigenbasis ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]). A self-adjoint operator's unitary group is strongly continuous, preserves its domain and commutes with it, and is differentiable on domain vectors ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]).

[F5] A continuous Banach-valued curve on a compact interval is Bochner integrable; its primitive has the curve as derivative, including one-sided endpoint derivatives, and the integral obeys the norm bound and linearity ([[lem-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus-for-banach-valued-continuous-curves]], [[thm-bochner-integrability-criterion]], [[lem-bochner-integral-norm-inequality]], [[lem-linearity-of-the-bochner-integral]]). Bounded linear maps commute with such integrals: this holds for simple approximants by linearity and passes to their $L^1$ limits by the map's norm bound.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; prove finite-photon graph vertex bounds, integrate vertices in chronological order, sum in the graph norm and identify the resulting strong solution with the self-adjoint evolution.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Free flow and vertex bounds] Diagonalizing the finite Hermitian $H_a$ and using [F3], [F4] gives $U_0(t)=e^{itH_a/\hbar}\otimes e^{itH_f/\hbar}$. Thus $U_0(t)$ preserves each $\mathcal K_m$, commutes with $F$ on $\mathcal G$, and is isometric and strongly continuous for the graph norm: both $U_0(t)x$ and $FU_0(t)x=U_0(t)Fx$ are continuous. On $\mathcal K_m$, the finite-sector extension of $B$ from [F2] satisfies $\|Bx\|\le|\eta_0|\gamma\sqrt{m+1}\|x\|$ and takes values in $\mathcal K_{m+1}$. Its free conjugate therefore satisfies $\|V(t)x\|\le|\eta_0|\gamma\sqrt{m+1}\|x\|$. The factor $|\eta_0|$ is included exactly once in this bound; $\gamma$ and $C$ contain no coupling. [F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

1.2 [Cutoff commutator and graph-domain extension] For $g$ supported in $\{0<\varepsilon\le\Lambda\}$, $\varepsilon g\in\mathfrak h$ and $\|\varepsilon g\|\le\Lambda\|g\|$. On symmetric elementary tensors with factors in $D(\varepsilon)$, the sector multiplier and creation formula give $[H_f,A_+(g)]=A_+(\varepsilon g)$. For contraction the removed factor contributes $-\langle\varepsilon u,g\rangle=-\langle u,\varepsilon g\rangle$, so $[H_f,A_-(g)]=-A_-(\varepsilon g)$. These identities extend to every finite-photon graph vector, with no claim that all of $F_0$ lies in $D(H_f)$. Indeed, in sector $n$ first cut each mode to $\varepsilon\le R$; dominated convergence in the Euclidean representation [F3] gives convergence of both the vector and its energy multiplier. On that cutoff subspace, energy is bounded by $nR$, so finite sums of elementary cutoff tensors, symmetrized, approximate in graph norm by tensor density. This supplies a graph core in each $\mathcal G_m$. The field and its candidate commutator are bounded on $\mathcal K_m$ by [F2], with respective bounds $2\sqrt{m+1}\|g\|$ and $2\Lambda\sqrt{m+1}\|g\|$. Applying the core identity to a graph-approximating sequence makes the output and its energy image converge; closedness of $H_f$ proves graph-domain preservation and the identity on the limit. Hence for $x\in\mathcal G_m$, $Bx\in\mathcal G_{m+1}$ and
$$FBx=BFx+Q_Bx,\qquad Q_B:=\eta_0\sum_jD_j\otimes\bigl(A_+(\varepsilon g_j)-A_-(\varepsilon g_j)\bigr),\qquad \|Q_Bx\|\le|\eta_0|\gamma\Lambda\sqrt{m+1}\|x\|.$$
[F2, F3, algebra, construct]

1.3 [Conjugated commutator and graph continuity] Since $F$ commutes with $U_0(t)$, step 1.2 gives on $\mathcal G_m$
$$FV(t)x=V(t)Fx+Q(t)x,\qquad Q(t):=U_0(t)Q_BU_0(-t),$$
with $\|Q(t)x\|\le|\eta_0|\gamma\Lambda\sqrt{m+1}\|x\|$. The conjugations in $Q(t)$ are retained. Equivalently, the sector formulas give $D_j(t)=e^{itH_a/\hbar}D_je^{-itH_a/\hbar}$ and $g_j(t)=e^{it\varepsilon/\hbar}g_j$, with
$$V(t)=\eta_0\sum_jD_j(t)\otimes\phi(g_j(t)),\qquad Q(t)=\eta_0\sum_jD_j(t)\otimes\bigl(A_+(\varepsilon g_j(t))-A_-(\varepsilon g_j(t))\bigr).$$
The same positive phase occurs in the annihilation vector argument because that argument is conjugate-linear, as in [F2]. The resulting graph bound is
$$\|V(t)x\|_{\mathcal G}\le|\eta_0|\gamma\sqrt{m+1}\bigl(\|Fx\|+(1+\Lambda)\|x\|\bigr).$$
Thus $V(t):\mathcal G_m\to\mathcal G_{m+1}$ is uniformly bounded in $t$ for these graph norms. Strong graph continuity of $U_0$, the fixed graph-bounded $B$ between these spaces, and the expression $U_0(t)BU_0(-t)x$ show that $t\mapsto V(t)x$ is graph continuous. On the full $\mathcal G$, [F1] and the graph isometry of $U_0$ additionally give $\|V(t)x\|\le K\|x\|_{\mathcal G}$ for one finite $K$ independent of $t$, and strong continuity as a map $\mathcal G\to\mathcal K$. No global map $V(t):\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ is asserted. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 [Chronological products and their graph bounds] Define $P_n(t_1,\ldots,t_n):=V(t_n)\cdots V(t_1)\Psi_0$, with $P_0=\Psi_0$. At the $k$-th vertex, the earlier product is in $\mathcal G_{k-1}$, so steps 1.1 and 1.3 give a factor $|\eta_0|\gamma\sqrt k$ in its Hilbert bound. Consequently $P_n\in\mathcal G_n$ and $\|P_n\|\le(|\eta_0|\gamma)^n\sqrt{n!}$. The graph commutator gives recursively $\|FP_k\|\le|\eta_0|\gamma\sqrt k(\|FP_{k-1}\|+\Lambda\|P_{k-1}\|)$; since $F\Psi_0=0$, induction yields $\|FP_n\|\le n\Lambda(|\eta_0|\gamma)^n\sqrt{n!}$. Each product is jointly continuous in its time variables for the graph norm: at each stage use strong graph continuity of the next $V$ on a fixed vector and its uniform graph bound to control the changing previous vector. For $n=0$ the Hilbert bound is $1$ and the energy bound is $0$, including when $|\eta_0|\gamma=0$. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.3, algebra, induction]

2.2 [Graph Bochner terms and the genuine recurrence] The graph space $\mathcal G$ is Banach: a graph-Cauchy sequence has limits of both the vectors and their $F$ images in the Hilbert space, and closedness of $F$ identifies them as a graph limit. Each $\mathcal G_n$ is closed in it. Step 2.1 and [F5] therefore make every iterated chronological integral a Bochner integral in $\mathcal G_n$. Its graph and Hilbert norm bounds follow by integrating the preceding product bounds over the simplex; the volume is $t^n/n!$, obtained recursively from $\int_0^t s^{n-1}/(n-1)!\,ds=t^n/n!$. Each factor of the integral contributes $1/\hbar$, giving
$$\|\Psi_n(t)\|\le\frac{(|\eta_0|Ct)^n}{\sqrt{n!}},\qquad \|F\Psi_n(t)\|\le\frac{n\Lambda(|\eta_0|Ct)^n}{\sqrt{n!}}.$$
For $n=0$ these bounds mean $1$ and $0$. Integrating the latest vertex last gives the actual left-vertex recurrence
$$\Psi_{n+1}(t)=\frac1{i\hbar}\int_0^tV(s)\Psi_n(s)\,ds.$$
For fixed $s$, move $V(s)$ through the inner integral as a bounded linear map $\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal G_{n+1}$ by [F5]; the earlier vertices have times below $s$, with $V(s)$ on the left. This also proves graph continuity of each term, and proves (a) and graph-domain membership in (b). [F3, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

3.1 [Uniform graph convergence] Fix $T<\infty$ and put $a:=|\eta_0|CT$. The graph majorant is $\sum_{n\ge0}(1+n\Lambda)a^n/\sqrt{n!}$. For $a>0$ the ratio of consecutive scalar terms tends to zero: it is $a(1+(n+1)\Lambda)/((1+n\Lambda)\sqrt{n+1})$. It is eventually at most $1/2$, proving convergence by a geometric tail comparison. If $a=0$, every positive-order term is zero and only the zeroth term remains. Thus the series converges uniformly for $0\le t\le T$ in the Banach graph space, and its sum $\Psi(t)$ is graph continuous and belongs to $D(H)=\mathcal G$. [step 2.2, algebra]

3.2 [Integral equation and Hilbert derivative] The uniform bound $\|V(s)x\|\le K\|x\|_{\mathcal G}$ from step 1.3 makes $V(s)\sum_{n\le M}\Psi_n(s)$ converge uniformly in Hilbert norm on $[0,T]$ to $V(s)\Psi(s)$. This limiting curve is continuous by graph continuity of $\Psi$, strong continuity of $V:\mathcal G\to\mathcal K$, and the same uniform bound. Sum the recurrences of step 2.2 and use the Bochner norm inequality [F5] to pass to the limit in their Hilbert integrals. The result is $\Psi(t)=\Psi_0+(i\hbar)^{-1}\int_0^tV(s)\Psi(s)\,ds$. The Banach-valued fundamental theorem now gives $\Psi\in C^1([0,T];\mathcal K)$, with the right derivative at zero, and $i\hbar\Psi'(t)=V(t)\Psi(t)$, $\Psi(0)=\Psi_0$. Along with step 3.1 this proves (b); graph continuity is used for domain control, while the differential equation is a Hilbert-space derivative. [F5, step 1.3, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

4.1 [Identification with the self-adjoint dynamics] Put $Y(t):=U_0(-t)\Psi(t)$. It is graph continuous and belongs to $D(H)$. The difference quotient splits into the difference of the free group on the fixed domain vector $\Psi(t)$ and the free group times the difference quotient of $\Psi$, so [F4] and step 3.2 justify the product derivative in Hilbert norm. Thus $i\hbar Y'=H_0Y+U_0(-t)V(t)\Psi=H_0Y+BY=HY$ and $Y(0)=\Psi_0$. By [F1], [F4], the Stone curve $e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0$ is another strong domain-valued solution because $\Psi_0\in\mathcal G=D(H)$. For their difference $w$, symmetry of $H$ gives
$$\frac d{dt}\|w(t)\|^2=2\operatorname{Re}\langle w'(t),w(t)\rangle=2\operatorname{Re}\left(-\frac i\hbar\langle Hw(t),w(t)\rangle\right)=0.$$
Both initial values agree, so $w=0$, proving (c) for every finite $t\ge0$. [F1, F4, step 3.1, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 [Tail, vacuum and zero branches] By step 4.1 and unitarity, the truncation error at time $t$ equals in norm the interaction-picture tail, so it is at most $\sum_{n\ge N}(|\eta_0|Ct)^n/\sqrt{n!}$; for $0\le t\le T$ this is at most the stated $T$ tail, proving (d). The vacuum zeroth term has $F\Psi_0=0$ and norm one. At $t=0$ all positive-order integrals vanish. If $\eta_0=0$, or if $\gamma=0$ (all contributing $D_j$ or $g_j$ zero), then $B=V=0$, all positive-order terms vanish, the interaction-picture sum is exactly $\Psi_0$, and the tail is zero for every $N\ge1$. The argument supplies finite-time convergence and the actual self-adjoint evolution, with the original scope limitations retained. [F3, F4, step 2.2, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Golden-rule coefficient approximate identity

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Chapter 13 Sections 13.5-13.9 pp. 180-190 (perturbation expansion, harmonic perturbations and spontaneous emission)

S. Pratt, Lecture Notes on Quantum Mechanics (Michigan State University, PHY 851/852; retrieved via the Internet Archive snapshot of 2024-04-21), Chapter 6 Sections 6.8-6.9 pp. 95-97 (time-dependent perturbation theory and Fermi's golden rule)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\hbar>0$.

**(a) The golden-rule kernel.** For $t>0$ define
$$K_t(x):=\frac1{\hbar^2t}\Bigl|\int_0^te^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb R .$$
Then $K_t$ is continuous, nonnegative and even, and for $x\ne0$
$$K_t(x)=\frac{4\sin^2\bigl(xt/(2\hbar)\bigr)}{x^2t},\qquad K_t(0)=\frac t{\hbar^2};$$
moreover for every $\delta>0$ and every $x$ with $|x|\ge\delta$,
$$K_t(x)\le\frac4{x^2t}\le\frac4{\delta^2t},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}.$$

**(b) Approximate identity.** Let $J\in L^1(\mathbb R)$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and let $\Delta\in\mathbb R$.
If the representative $J$ is continuous at $\Delta$
([[def-continuity-real]]), then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)J(\Delta+x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J(\Delta)$$
([[def-limits-at-infinity]]).

**(c) First-order emission coefficient.** Adopt the objects and hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]: $\alpha>0$, the
transverse space $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$, the cutoff $\Lambda>0$, the vectors
$g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,$$
the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ and the coupling
$\eta_0\in\mathbb R$. Let $v_a,v_b$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of $H_a$ with
$H_av_a=E_av_a$, $H_av_b=E_av_b$, and let $\Delta:=E_a-E_b>0$. Put
$$c_j:=\langle D_jv_a,v_b\rangle\ (\mathbb C^d\text{ inner product}),\qquad M:=\sum_{j=1}^Jc_jg_j\in\mathfrak h,$$
and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_b(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf 1_A(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k, \qquad A\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
and for $t\ge0$ the amplitude
$$A_b(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}M(k)\int_0^te^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds .$$
Then:

(i) $\nu_b$ is a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$\nu_b(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$, and
$$\int_{\mathbb R}f\,d\nu_b=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k$$
for every Borel $f\ge0$;

(ii) $A_b(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$ for every $t\ge0$, and
for $t>0$,
$$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\eta_0^2t\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E).$$
At $t=0$ the amplitude is zero, so its squared norm is zero; no $K_0$ is used.

(iii) if $\nu_b=J_b\lambda$ for some $J_b\in L^1(\lambda)$ with $J_b=0$
$\lambda$-a.e. on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$ and the representative $J_b$
continuous at $\Delta$, then for $0<\Delta<\Lambda$
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\frac{2\pi\eta_0^2}{\hbar}J_b(\Delta);$$
if instead $\Delta>\Lambda$, then the same limit exists and equals $0$. The
boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is not asserted.

*Motivation and scope.* In the cutoff dipole model of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] the vector
$A_b(\cdot,t)$ is the explicit single-vertex amplitude with the atom passing
from $v_a$ to $v_b$ and one photon emitted; $\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2$ is the
corresponding first-order photon coefficient, and (iii) is the golden-rule
limit of that coefficient divided by $t$. This item computes only the limit of
the explicit coefficient, under the stated hypotheses on the spectral density
$J_b$. It asserts no approximation of the exact model evolution, no all-time or
weak-coupling limit, no Markov property and no exact exponential decay, and it
reports no measurement or empirical rate. The parameter $\hbar$, the coupling
$\eta_0$ and the matrices $D_j$ enter as mathematical normalisation data of the
model; their physical identification is a separate assumption.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space, let $H^{\otimes n}$ be its completed tensor powers with
the unitaries $U_\pi$ and projections $P_\pm^{(n)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]. Fix $n\ge2$ and vectors $u_1,\ldots,u_n\in H$, and let
$$S(u_1,\dots,u_n):=\frac1{\sqrt{n!}}\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, u_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\sigma(n)}$$
be the Slater vector of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]. This
example verifies concretely that:

(a) for every $u\in H$ the antisymmetrised two-particle tensor vanishes,
$$P_-^{(2)}(u\otimes u)=0,$$
because the transposition $\tau$ of the two tensor factors satisfies
$U_\tau(u\otimes u)=u\otimes u$ and $P_-^{(2)}=\tfrac12(\mathrm{id}-U_\tau)$;

(b) consequently the Slater vector with a repeated orbital is the zero vector,
$$S(u,u)=\frac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(u\otimes u-u\otimes u\bigr)=0\qquad(u\in H),$$
and the norm-one conclusion of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] (a)
does not apply to the degenerate list $(u,u)$: orthonormality of $u_1,\dots,u_n$
is an essential hypothesis, not a convenience; for orthonormal $u_1,u_2$ one
has $\|S(u_1,u_2)\|=1$;

(c) exclusion is a property of the *state* and not only of basis labels:
for $H=\mathbb C^2$ with orthonormal basis $e_1,e_2$ and the non-basis vector
$u:=e_1+e_2$ the antisymmetric part still vanishes. Indeed $u\otimes u
=e_1\otimes e_1+e_1\otimes e_2+e_2\otimes e_1+e_2\otimes e_2$, and
$P_-^{(2)}$ annihilates the two diagonal tensors while exchanging the two
crossed tensors with opposite sign, so $P_-^{(2)}(u\otimes u)=0$;

(d) in the actual tensor space $H^{\otimes2}$, the two-particle antisymmetric sector $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(2)}$ contains no **nonzero** vector of the form $P_-^{(2)}(u\otimes u)$: every repeated-orbital projection is zero, and zero belongs to this sector as it does to every linear subspace. Thus a nonvanishing antisymmetric two-particle vector cannot be built from two copies of the same one-particle vector. This sector is distinct from the symmetric two-particle sector of the bosonic $F(H)$ in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]].

The antisymmetric sector and its projection are mathematical objects; as
recorded in the cited suppliers, selecting this sector for a species is a
postulate and no spin-statistics statement is proved here.
